newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen steady to lower, pork bellies lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen steady to lower, pork bellies lower.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent per lb lower while pork belly futures were called 0.250 to 1.000 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

Most analysts anticipate carryover selling in hog futures, especially in deferred months. Pressure is seen into the hog report at the end of the month which is expected to show increased hog numbers, they said.
However, nearbys may again be supported by the strong cash pork product market and steady cash hog indications. The lean index was also up, they said.
Hog slaughter up from a year ago while cash pork product values are rising shows a demand curve change, they added.

But the larger pace of slaughter is bearish to pork belly futures and futures are seen showing further losses after closing down the daily permissible limit in all months Thursday. Hog slaughter is running about three percent above a year ago, they said.
Traders were also looking for futures to invert with cash seasonally to move product out of storage during the peak summer demand.
However, analysts generally consider futures oversold and look for evening up ahead of the weekend to provide underlying support. Light storage stocks is also supportive, they said.
